newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt moves ahead with church restoration project.
newsitem.headline: Egypt moves ahead with church restoration project.

text.p: The Egyptian antiquities department announced on Tuesday it was looking for a contractor to restore one of Egypt's oldest and best known churches, the Hanging Church in Old Cairo.
The church, which is probably 1,300 years old, has had severe structural problems for years, compounded by the side effects of the high water table in the area.

The Supreme Council of Antiquities said it was inviting contractors to submit prequalification documents for a project to restore the church, the remains of the Roman fort supporting it and the Coptic Museum nearby.
The council has set aside about 25 million pounds ($7.4 million) for the restoration of the church alone.

The church, probably founded in the late 7th century but first mentioned in the 9th century, takes its name from the way it rests on the bastions of the Roman fort. It suffered badly in the Cairo earthquake of October 1992.
Many of the walls are cracked and the priests say it is in danger of collapsing without quick restoration. Some of the low-lying parts are flooded with slimy green water.

The new secretary general of the antiquities council, Ali Hassan, said it had taken longer than expected to prepare the restoration plans because the council wants the job done properly. The contractors will try to match original materials.
The council said it was giving companies 15 days to submit the prequalification documents. They must find a subcontractor specialising in ground water control, it added.
